by_task.when: Federal exemptions are an allowable namespace for the case and an estate asset is being classified.
by_task.procedure: Check 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5) independently for every asset. It covers the debtor's interest in any property, so retain it alongside every applicable specific federal or state exemption; its dollar ceiling limits the protected amount rather than EC eligibility.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not use § 522(d)(5) when federal exemptions are unavailable, and do not omit it merely because the asset has another exemption or exceeds the statutory ceiling.

by_task.when: Federal exemptions are allowable and an estate asset is being valued.
by_task.procedure: Include 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5) independently for any property, alongside every applicable specific exemption. For each debtor, the ceiling is $1,475 plus up to $13,950 of that debtor's unused § 522(d)(1) amount. Determine the unused amount from the supplied facts, apply the resulting ceiling to that debtor's interest, and sum the protected interests to report the final amount for the whole asset; with equal joint ownership, calculate the two halves separately rather than returning one half-interest.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not use § 522(d)(5) if federal exemptions are unavailable. Do not omit it because a specific exemption applies, treat $1,475 as the full ceiling when § 522(d)(1) remains unused, or double a ceiling without first applying it to each debtor's interest.

by_task.when: Pennsylvania exemptions are allowable and the debtor has an interest in an estate asset.
by_task.procedure: Include 42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8123 as an independent alternative for property of the judgment debtor, while retaining any applicable particular-property exemption. The $300 limit restricts value protected, not whether the citation is eligible in EC.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not treat § 8123 as replacing a specific exemption, and do not exclude an asset merely because its value exceeds $300.

by_task.when: Pennsylvania exemptions are allowable and the debtor or debtors own an estate asset.
by_task.procedure: Include 42 Pa. Cons. Stat. § 8123 independently for the property and retain any applicable particular-property exemption. Protect up to $300 of each spouse's interest and sum those interests for the whole asset, so a sole debtor has at most $300 and two equal joint debtors have at most $600, subject to the asset's value.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not reject § 8123 because the asset exceeds its ceiling or because another exemption applies. Apply § 8124(a)(1) only to wearing apparel, not to firearms or jewelry merely because they are personal items.

by_task.when: Oregon exemptions are allowable and the asset is personal property.
by_task.procedure: Check and retain Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(p) independently of category-specific Oregon exemptions. Its $400 ceiling limits protected value; it does not make a higher-value personal asset ineligible for the citation.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not apply this personal-property alternative to real property, and do not omit it because a clothing, household-goods, vehicle, animal, or other specific Oregon exemption also applies.

by_task.when: Oregon exemptions are allowable and the named asset is personal property.
by_task.procedure: Include Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(p) independently alongside every applicable category-specific exemption. For this asset-level output, report the lesser of the whole asset's value and $400.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not apply § 18.345(1)(p) to real property, omit it because a specific Oregon exemption applies, or double the $400 whole-asset result merely because two debtors jointly own the asset.

by_task.when: Illinois exemptions are allowable and the asset is debtor-owned personal property held for personal rather than business use.
by_task.procedure: Check 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) independently for the asset and retain it alongside any applicable motor-vehicle, necessary-apparel, or prescribed-health-aid provision. Its $4,000 ceiling limits protected equity rather than EC eligibility.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not apply § 12-1001(b) to real or business-use property. Do not classify jewelry as necessary wearing apparel under § 12-1001(a) merely because it is worn.

by_task.when: Illinois exemptions are allowable and the asset is debtor-owned personal property used personally rather than for business.
by_task.procedure: Include 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) independently alongside any applicable motor-vehicle, necessary-apparel, or prescribed-health-aid exemption. Protect up to $4,000 of each debtor's interest and sum the protected interests for the whole asset; under equal joint ownership this yields at most $8,000, subject to the asset's value.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not apply § 12-1001(b) to real or business-use property, omit it because a specific exemption also applies, or classify a necklace, watch, or other jewelry as necessary wearing apparel under § 12-1001(a).

by_task.when: Arizona exemptions are allowable and the asset is a firearm, motor vehicle, apparel item, or item of jewelry.
by_task.procedure: Classify by the statutory category: firearms under Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(10), each motor vehicle as a candidate under § 33-1125(8), wearing apparel under § 33-1125(1), and only engagement or wedding rings under § 33-1125(4). In EC, a value or aggregate ceiling limits protection rather than citation eligibility, and the one-vehicle language does not require final portfolio allocation among separately listed vehicle candidates.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not reject an otherwise matching firearm or vehicle solely for exceeding its ceiling. Do not treat a pendant, bracelet, or other non-apparel adornment as wearing apparel, and do not extend the ring exemption to jewelry that is not an engagement or wedding ring.

by_task.when: Arizona exemptions are allowable and the asset is a firearm, motor vehicle, apparel item, or item of jewelry.
by_task.procedure: Classify before valuing: use Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(10) for firearms up to $2,000, § 33-1125(8) for each separately listed motor-vehicle candidate up to $15,000, § 33-1125(1) for actual wearing apparel up to $500, and § 33-1125(4) only for engagement or wedding rings up to $2,000. For each eligible alternative, report the lesser of the whole asset's value and its stated ceiling.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not treat a pendant, bracelet, watch, or other adornment as wearing apparel, extend the ring exemption to jewelry that is not an engagement or wedding ring, or perform a final allocation between separately listed vehicle candidates.

by_task.when: Arizona exemptions are allowable and the asset is a residence, homestead-sale proceeds, or property owned by married debtors.
by_task.procedure: For a qualifying occupied homestead, use Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1101(A); for qualifying identifiable sale proceeds, separately test § 33-1101(C). Treat § 33-1101(B) and § 33-1121 as ceiling or spouse-administration rules, not independent asset exemptions.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not attach § 33-1101(B) or § 33-1121 to an asset merely because the debtors are married or the asset qualifies under another substantive exemption.

by_task.when: Producing the final EC mapping after evaluating the allowable statutes for all listed assets.
by_task.procedure: For each asset separately, take the union of all independently eligible citation alternatives and emit each citation once. Return an empty array only after every applicable specific and general-property alternative has been checked.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not repeat a citation within an asset's array, copy one asset's category citations into another asset, or replace a specific exemption with a general alternative.

by_task.when: Federal exemptions are allowable and the asset is household furnishings or goods, wearing apparel, an appliance, a book, an animal, a crop, or a musical instrument held for personal, family, or household use.
by_task.procedure: Apply 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(3) and report the lesser of the whole asset's value and the $700 per-item ceiling. Retain any independently applicable § 522(d)(5) alternative.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not report the asset's full value under § 522(d)(3) when it exceeds $700, and do not apply this listed-category exemption to a firearm merely because the firearm is personal property.

by_task.when: Illinois exemptions are allowable and the named asset is a motor vehicle held for personal use.
by_task.procedure: Include 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(c) as a separate alternative and report the lesser of the whole vehicle's value and $2,400. Also retain § 12-1001(b) when its personal-property conditions are met.
by_task.avoid_when: Do not substitute the $4,000 other-property ceiling for the $2,400 motor-vehicle ceiling, double the motor-vehicle amount merely because there are two debtors, or make a final allocation between separately listed vehicle candidates.
